title: Inspect Gmail history cursor serialization and ID precision

findings.summary: Existing test only asserts message metadata.history_id, not cursor.anchor encode/decode.
findings.affected: P051/P052 must not treat uint64 cursor round-trip as already proved
findings.action: Reuse /work/out/fixtures/gmail-cursor-neutral.json; do not duplicate the metadata test

findings.summary: Local historyId() refuses 0 and allows 21-40 digit strings; Google discovery types these fields as string uint64 (0..2^64-1).
findings.evidence: packages/connector-gmail/src/state.ts:64-68; Gmail discovery revision 20260903; executed identifier cases history-zero, history-2-pow-64, local-21-digit-anchor
findings.affected: Accepted non-uint64 anchors still round-trip as strings and compare via BigInt
findings.action: P051/P052 decide whether to clamp to uint64 or keep the local bound

findings.summary: pageToken empty string is source_schema, not null.
findings.affected: A provider empty nextPageToken would refuse the batch rather than end pagination
findings.action: Keep documented; Gmail docs describe omitted nextPageToken

findings.summary: JSON string history IDs beyond MAX_SAFE_INTEGER round-trip; JSON numbers are refused; sync ordering uses BigInt.
findings.evidence: roundtrip-report.json precision and cases sync-uint64-max-anchor, sync-beyond-safe-integer, history-json-number; connector.ts:278,292
